claims.statement: Tom Allen and Joe Goss, who had signed articles to fight for the English championship, were both arrested on bench warrants on the eve of the fight.
claims.excerpt: both men were arrested on the eve of the fight upon bench warrants

claims.statement: Tom Allen was in America in 1867.
claims.excerpt: At that time (1867) Tom Allen was at his very best

claims.statement: In 1867 Tom Allen was about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighed about 164 pounds.
claims.excerpt: fully 5 feet 10 inches, and about 164 pounds.

claims.statement: Soon after arriving in America, Tom Allen was matched with Mike McCoole; McCoole's friends stopped the fight with ball cartridge while Allen was winning.
claims.excerpt: soon after his arrival in America he made a match with Mike McCoole, a man almost big enough to eat him

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Joe Goss in America for the championship of the world; Goss's armed backers forced the referee to give the decision to Goss when Goss was losing.
claims.excerpt: that worthy was induced to give his decision in favor of the man who would in all probability have lost

fights.excerpt: soon after his arrival in America he made a match with Mike McCoole, a man almost big enough to eat him
fights.notes: Stopped by McCoole's friends with ball cartridge while Allen was winning (Clark's account). Date approximate.

fights.excerpt: The men, of course, fought under the recognized London Prize Ring Rules
fights.notes: Year not given in this article. Decision given to Goss after the referee was pressured by Goss's backers.

notes: Clark's recollections in Billy Murphy's article. The arrest story conflicts with article 234, which has Allen and Goss fighting a draw on March 5, 1867.
